changelog: setup_shotgun.sh --func: the conda env ngamp-func was created with python 3.10, but bioconda builds humann 3.9 for python 3.12 only, so 'humann_databases' stopped with "No module named 'humann'". The env now uses python 3.12, is checked by importing humann and metaphlan, and a broken env is rebuilt. Nothing else changes; no backend restart needed.

previous.changelog: Shotgun: function profiles with HUMAnN 3.9 (opt-in, step 4 'Function (HUMAnN)'). MetaPhlAn 4.1.1 (vJun23) and HUMAnN 3.9 against full UniRef90 give MetaCyc pathways (with coverage), KEGG KO and EC per sample, plus genes of interest in three editable sets — gut (SCFA, bile acids, TMA, B12, folate), food (lactic acid, bacteriocins, biogenic amines, proteolysis) and environment (nitrogen, sulfur, methane, degradation) — each with the genera carrying it. The report adds Key findings on page 1, function QC, a MetaPhlAn vs Kraken 2 cross-check, functional diversity (Shannon, KO PCoA, PERMANOVA) and MaAsLin 3 on pathways, KO and panel genes; the chart editor gets a Function tab. Nanopore reads are cut into 300 bp pieces (beta). A job with Function on needs ~25 GB RAM and runs alone: it waits for running jobs, and later jobs show 'Waiting — HUMAnN job running' and start by themselves afterwards. Install: bash setup_shotgun.sh --func --func-db-dir DIR (~50 GB; nextapp: /mnt/e/ngamp-db/humann). Function is off by default; every shotgun report now also opens with a Key findings box (host share, top genera, AMR genes and carriers, genome bins). Backend restart required.
